C003.text: Commission: Expressive spoken storyteller with an invented voice (Kikuyu, Kamba, Kiswahili) (STORY-KIK-KAM-SWA).

C004.text: Product: one agent that invents coherent stories and speaks them with the language character of each language in a voice that is no corpus presenter

C005.text: Task: story generation and expressive multilingual speech rendering — radio storytelling register, three languages.

Design v2: language-balanced curriculum, dense identity conditioning hypothesis, padded-text masking, delayed-codebook flush and complete cross-language rendered checks; no claim of convergence..

C023.text: Training: a codec language model (text characters → delayed Mimi frames, eight codebooks) trained from scratch. Rendered dev prompts are measured with the same discoverable-spectrum columns as the corpus; the per-feature divergence between generated and baseline distributions is the spectral-behaviour similarity, and where it is shifted the next curriculum up-weights the under-covered side of that feature (spectral feedback). The identity gate embeds each rendering and requires its cosine to every corpus-derived speaker comparator to stay below the threshold; comparators live in memory only.

C037.text: Spectral-behaviour similarity is an instrument, not naturalness: a rendering can match the corpus distributions and still sound wrong. Native-listener ratings on unseen stories are required and are recorded as pending.

C038.text: The identity gate is scoped to corpus-derived speaker representations of this estate; it is not a claim of global uniqueness over all humans.

C039.text: No pretrained Kikamba voice exists as a comparator; the Kikamba baseline is the corpus distribution alone.
